staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged htslib checkout. The benchmark metadata names vulnerable commit `23a67495...`, but the live staged tree used for line mapping is the earlier ancestor `01830d77...`; it contains the same vulnerable xpack logic and matches the staged `patch.diff` hunk that adds the missing `nval`/`nbits` validation.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42492011 (htslib): Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 4 found by fuzz target hts_open_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42492011
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The staged 91-byte witness is a malformed CRAM 1.5 file. `view_sam()` reaches `sam_read1_cram()`, `cram_get_seq()`, and `cram_first_slice()`, which calls `cram_decode_compression_header()` for the first slice's compression header. In that record-encoding map, a duplicate `IN` entry is classified as `E_BYTE_ARRAY`, its codec varint resolves to `E_XPACK`, and `cram_decoder_init()` dispatches the entry's payload into `cram_xpack_decode_init()`. That initializer allocates a 2168-byte `cram_codec`, parses attacker-controlled `nval` from the xpack header, and immediately uses `nval` as the loop bound for storing entries into `c->u.xpack.rmap[256]`. The only in-loop check is `if (v >= 256) return NULL;`, which constrains each stored symbol value but never bounds the destination index or `nval`. As a result, writes past `rmap[255]` overrun adjacent codec state and, in the reproduced run, continue until AddressSanitizer reports a heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4 at `cram_codecs.c:1415`, 0 bytes to the right of the 2168-byte allocation created at line 1391. The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by rejecting malformed xpack headers with `nval > 256` (and invalid `nbits`) before the write loop.

source.description: First project parser step on the crashing path that materializes the current record-encoding-map entry's codec id from attacker-controlled bytes.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a 91-byte CRAM 1.5 file. The saved ASan stack later reaches `cram_xpack_decode_init()` through `cram_decoder_init()`, so for the crashing `IN` entry this varint decodes to `E_XPACK` rather than `E_NULL` or another codec.

root_cause.description: The xpack initializer uses attacker-controlled `nval` as the number of reverse-map writes without the missing `nval <= 256` guard later added by the patch.
root_cause.note: Pre-patch, the code validates each decoded `v` and only performs its remaining malformed-header check after the loop; nothing constrains `nval` against the fixed `rmap[256]` extent before `i` is used as the write index.

sink.code: c->u.xpack.rmap[i] = v; // reverse map: e.g 0-3 to P,A,C,K
sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. This 4-byte store uses loop index `i` as an `rmap[256]` subscript, so once the unchecked loop reaches an out-of-range index the write overruns the xpack codec object.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `WRITE of size 4` at `cram_codecs.c:1415` on address `0x61d000001cf8`, 0 bytes to the right of the 2168-byte region allocated at `cram_xpack_decode_init:1391`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This xpack-header varint parses attacker-controlled `nval`, the loop bound later used to decide how many entries are written into `rmap`.

parser_admitted.description: The input has already been admitted as sequence/CRAM, `sam_read1_cram()` / `cram_get_seq()` have reached the first slice, and the compression-header parser is now decoding the record-encoding map that contains the crashing xpack `IN` entry.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation; the chain is grounded only in the staged source, patch, saved ASan traces, and reproduction report.

Stage 02 does not execute the fixed image, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains false even though `patch.diff` inserts the exact missing `nval`/`nbits` validation before the crashing loop.

The benchmark metadata commit pair does not match the live staged checkout. All file paths and line numbers below are grounded in `_work/src/htslib` at `01830d77...`, the snapshot Stage 01 actually used to reproduce this crash.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness wraps the staged 91-byte witness in an in-memory file, `hts_hopen()` recognizes CRAM, and `view_sam()` drives `sam_read1_cram()` into first-slice CRAM decoding.

The first slice's record-encoding map is parsed; a duplicate `IN` entry is classified as `E_BYTE_ARRAY`, its codec varint resolves to `E_XPACK`, and the entry is dispatched through `cram_decoder_init()`.
Xpack initialization allocates a `cram_codec`, parses attacker-controlled `nval` from the xpack header, and uses `nval` as the number of reverse-map writes into `rmap[256]`.

Because the loop only checks each stored symbol value (`v < 256`) and never bounds `nval` against the destination extent, `c->u.xpack.rmap[i] = v` overruns the codec object and ASan reports a 4-byte heap-buffer-overflow at line 1415.

fine_trace.note: Source. The record-encoding-map parser decodes the current entry's codec id from attacker-controlled bytes and advances `cp` past that varint. On the crashing path this value is `E_XPACK`, as shown by the later `cram_xpack_decode_init()` frame.

The next varint materializes the payload byte length for the same map entry. Because execution later reaches `cram_decoder_init()` instead of returning at the `size < 0 || endp - cp < size` guard, this size admits the attacker-controlled xpack header bytes passed downstream.

fine_trace.code:
} else if (key[0] == 'I' && key[1] == 'N') {
    ds_id = DS_IN; type = E_BYTE_ARRAY;
fine_trace.note: The current record-encoding-map key selects the `IN` data series and byte-array option for this entry. The reproduced run logs `Codec for key IN defined more than once` twice, so the crashing path passes through duplicate `IN` definitions rather than rejecting them.

fine_trace.code:
cram_codec *r = decode_init[codec](hdr, data, size, codec,
                                   option, version, vv);
fine_trace.note: With `codec = E_XPACK`, `data = cp`, the admitted `size`, and `option = E_BYTE_ARRAY`, `cram_decoder_init()` selects the xpack initializer for this `IN` entry. In the duplicate-key path, the caller frees the old DS_IN codec and still invokes this replacement decoder.

Xpack initialization allocates the codec object that will hold the reverse map. `cram_codecs.h` defines this object with `c->u.xpack.rmap[256]`, and the saved ASan allocation stack shows this `malloc(sizeof(*c))` created a 2168-byte heap region.
The second xpack-header varint materializes attacker-controlled `nval`, the number of mapping entries the loop will attempt to store into `rmap`.

Root cause. The loop uses untrusted `nval` as the number of writes into the fixed-size reverse map, but no pre-loop check enforces `c->u.xpack.nval <= 256`. The later malformed-header check only validates `nbits` and full payload consumption after the writes have already happened.

fine_trace.code:
uint32_t v = vv->varint_get32(&cp, endp, NULL);
if (v >= 256) return NULL;
fine_trace.note: Each iteration parses the next attacker-controlled table value and applies the only present guard in this loop. That guard rejects out-of-range symbol values, but it says nothing about whether the destination index `i` still fits the 256-entry `rmap`.

fine_trace.code: c->u.xpack.rmap[i] = v; // reverse map: e.g 0-3 to P,A,C,K
fine_trace.note: Sink. This statement uses `i` as the reverse-map subscript and writes four bytes to `rmap[i]`. Once `i` exceeds 255, the loop writes beyond the intended 256-entry table; in the reproduced run it continues until this store lands 0 bytes past the 2168-byte heap allocation from step 5, where ASan reports the heap-buffer-overflow WRITE.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch adds the exact missing `nval`/`nbits` validation before the xpack write loop, but Stage 02 does not execute the fixed image.

poc.trigger: The staged `poc` is a 91-byte CRAM 1.5 file. When `hts_open_fuzzer` decodes the first slice compression header, duplicate `IN` codec definitions are seen and the replacement `IN` entry is dispatched as `E_XPACK`; its xpack header carries an oversized `nval`, so `cram_xpack_decode_init()` keeps filling `rmap[i]` until ASan reports the 4-byte heap write.

format.name: CRAM 1.5
format.contract: A 91-byte CRAM 1.5 file whose first crashing slice compression header contains a later `IN` record-encoding-map entry that survives the duplicate-key replacement path, is dispatched as `E_XPACK`, and has an xpack header whose `nval` varint is large enough for the `rmap` fill loop to advance past the fixed 256-entry reverse map and reach the heap redzone of the 2168-byte `cram_codec` object.
